designSummary: Run chart and p-chart of 60-day completion by index-case month cohort: 12 baseline cohorts (2026) and 12 improvement cohorts (2027).
sampleSize: About 1,300 contacts a year give cohorts of about 100 contacts per index-case month. With a baseline near 71 percent, p-chart limits for cohorts of 100 are about 14 points either side, so single cohorts can show only large changes, but run chart rules detect a sustained 12-point improvement within five to six cohorts (retrieved simulation). A rise to 85 percent held for six cohorts would meet the shift rule by mid-2027. Equity subgroups (about 15 to 25 contacts a month each) are charted quarterly and described, not tested.
primaryAnalysis: Run chart of cohort completion with the baseline median; shift, trend and runs rules fixed in advance; p-chart with 3-sigma limits alongside.
secondaryAnalysis: Median days to completed evaluation per cohort; cascade losses per step; nurse hours per case; quarterly completion for shelter, shift-working and interpreter-needing contacts.
missingData: Cohorts are charted only after the missing-date check; contacts with a missing closure date after checking are counted as not completed and the number is reported.
multiplicity: One aim measure; the rest are descriptive.
software: Spreadsheet chart template maintained by the program epidemiologist.
overfittingGuards: Rules and baseline fixed before the first change
No re-baselining until a sustained shift
summary: Monthly cohorts of about 100 contacts; a sustained 12-point change detectable within about six cohorts.
